headline: The Desk's AI-generated satire now has one collision-free typography authority, immutable reviewed artwork, and exact production proof through Aug. 23.

items.title: The Desk satire now reads clearly without competing text layers
items.insight: Story art now reserves opaque masthead and caption zones while the page suppresses its former duplicate visible pull quote. Text-free source scenes and a single external caption layer make each joke legible without image-embedded labels, overlapping copy, or conflicting repetition.
items.evidence: 28/28 theme-and-viewport captures manually passed · production desktop and 390px mobile article inspection passed

items.title: Scheduled publishing preserves reviewed artwork by default
items.insight: Normal newsroom rebuilds now preserve complete art families, fail closed on partial families, and require an explicit refresh-art operation to replace reviewed files. The scheduled workflow also rejects any tracked Desk-art mutation, so a routine publish cannot silently regress a reviewed meme.
items.evidence: news-desk self-test 139/139 · publisher resilience 18/18 across 29 workflows · normal rebuild generated zero replacement cards

items.title: The improved satire shipped through the guarded content lane
items.insight: The exact candidate passed the scoped release gate and continuous integration, then production verification matched all twelve Desk pages, thirty-six assets, the Aug. 23 edition, and its five claim rows. A bounded fail-closed retry absorbs edge propagation without weakening exact-content verification.

followUps: Bind a compact rendered-pixel receipt to every newly generated Desk story before it becomes publishable.
Add a visual-diversity memory so recurring visual metaphors remain deliberate across editions.
blockers: The unrelated full-site identity lane remains held pending real-provider Obelisk evidence; the Desk content release is complete and verified.
